Definition

Read “R-3”.   Board note on the last part: , and are members of the set of all real numbers.

The 1-1 correspondence between and 3-d space is called 3-d rectangular coordinate system or Euclidean 3-space.

Explanation (added)

“1-1 correspondence” means every point of space gets exactly one triple and every triple names exactly one point. That is what lets geometry (points, surfaces) and algebra (triples, equations) be used interchangeably for the rest of the course.

Explanation (added)

Solving for shows the 2-D graph is a parabola opening downward with vertex ; setting gives the two -intercepts. The same idea — “the graph is the set of all points that satisfy the equation” — carries over to 3-D, but one equation in three unknowns leaves two degrees of freedom, so the picture is a two-dimensional sheet rather than a one-dimensional curve.

Explanation (added)

These slices are called traces (Stewart uses the word in §12.6). The slice is exactly the 2-D parabola from before, . Stacking the slices shows the surface is a trough made of identical parabolas sliding along a slanted line — a parabolic cylinder, tilted because of the term.

Explanation (added)

The same equation means different things depending on the space it lives in. In , a variable that does not appear in the equation is free: says nothing about , so the parabola is copied at every height and becomes a surface.

Every point on the sphere satisfies this equation, and every point of distance from is on the sphere. So its equation is:

Explanation (added)

This is the distance formula with the square root removed: “distance from to equals ”, squared on both sides. The two halves of the board’s sentence are the two directions of an “if and only if” — that is what it takes for an equation to be the equation of a set.
